_comment: What `layout/erc/run_erc.py` runs and what it asserts. One entry per
spec file: the item-11 supply spec, plus the controls that make its
clean verdict mean something.
`expect` is asserted field by field. A field absent from an `expect`
block is not checked; a field present and wrong fails the run with a
named mismatch. The point is that a re-run functions as a regression
test rather than a screenshot -- the same argument layout/drc/cells/
cells.json makes for the DRC deck.
`layout_sha256` pins the geometry every case is run against, so a
report can never silently belong to a different GDS than the one this
repo committed. It is the same value `klt erc` reports as
`provenance.input.content_hash`, and the same value
signoff/gf180-sar-adc.manifest.json pins for this block's DRC citation.
`expect.erc_finding_counts` is exhaustive: a rule missing from the map
is asserted to have fired ZERO times. That is what makes the supply
case's empty map the affirmative statement `no rule fired` rather than
`the rules we remembered to list did not fire`.
WHAT ISSUE #356 CHANGED HERE. The supply spec now declares `ties[]`,
so its zero `erc.missing_tie` is a COMPUTED verdict rather than an
uncomputed check -- `expect.spec_declares_ties` flipped to true and
`expect.erc_coverage_checked_rules` was added to assert that the tie
rule landed in `erc_coverage.checked` rather than being skipped. A
zero that comes from a skipped rule and a zero that comes from a rule
that ran are the same number in `erc_finding_counts`; only the
coverage list tells them apart, which is exactly the distinction this
directory spent #340 establishing.
The `tie-narrowed` known gap (B) is GONE, replaced by
`tie-wrong-implant`. That control declared the same `COMP n Nplus`
narrowing the supply spec now uses and reported 25 `erc.missing_tie`
from an EMPTY tap region -- a reproduction of the implant-free stream,
which this stream no longer is. Keeping it would have meant asserting
that the artifact and a byte-identical control disagree, which they
cannot. `tie-wrong-implant` is its successor and a strictly stronger
control: it moves the implant (32/0 -> 31/0) rather than the layout,
so its 25 findings come from a non-empty tap region that lands
outside every well.

cases.name: adc_block.supply
cases.claim: vdd and vss each resolve to exactly one electrical island, and every one of the 25 drawn Nwell islands carries an Nplus-marked tap that reaches vdd: zero erc.unconnected_net, zero erc.supply_short, zero erc.missing_tie -- with the tie rule CHECKED, not skipped

cases.name: adc_block.unconnected-net-control
cases.claim: the erc.unconnected_net rule is live -- a supply name nothing carries fires it exactly once

cases.name: adc_block.tie-bare.known-gap
cases.claim: a bare tap_layer is classified degenerate and skipped, not passed (klayout-tools#2199) -- which is why the supply spec's tie declaration MUST carry the tap_requires narrowing rather than naming COMP alone

cases.name: adc_block.tie-wrong-implant.control
cases.claim: the supply spec's zero erc.missing_tie could have been non-zero: the SAME tie declaration narrowed on Pplus 31/0 instead of Nplus 32/0 -- a non-empty implant this stream really draws, but only on the substrate ties outside every well -- reports all 25 wells untapped

cases.name: adc_block.no-devices.known-gap
cases.claim: without devices[], the comparator's poly load resistors read as wire and fuse vdd to XCMP.pon/XCMP.pop
